description: Stage 1 of plans/particle-family.md (#196): every airborne-particle row of every list is read into one of the seven size windows, a row nobody has read stops the merge instead of minting a substance, and every window always publishes its `Particulates` spelling as an alternative label. Measured against the five-list build of 2 September 2026 (944b274), where Stepwise's `Particulates, < 10 um` and `(mobile)` and AGRIBALYSE's `Particulates, diesel soot` and `Particulates, SPM` were four substances of their own with no window and no factor, and PM10 carried the plain spelling of no vendor. Stage 2: a particle flow of one size window that nobody characterises takes its nearest broader window's stated number, inside the compartment, before the compartment convention runs (data/particle-size-carry-rules.json); and Stepwise's two numbers for particles of unstated size are ruled 0.157 (data/lcia-factor-collision-rulings.json), which the above-ten fraction then takes. Measured against the build of 944b274 (2 September 2026), where the coarse band and the unsized total carried no consensus factor under either method.

expectations.title: Stepwise's plain `Particulates, < 10 um` lands on the flow this list publishes for PM10
expectations.comment: On the build of 944b274 this row minted `Particulates, < 10 Um`, a substance of its own beside `Particles (PM10)`, because the tool that writes particulate-flow-classes.json left Stepwise out of its sources while the list was unregistered and nobody put it back when #169 registered it. The reading existed all along; the row is in the table now, and the guard of this stage makes the omission a failing build rather than a silent substance.

expectations.title: PM10 from a mobile source is still PM10
expectations.comment: The second Stepwise stray. The source category is recorded and the window is the identity; Stepwise gives plain, mobile and stationary PM10 the same 0.535714286 kg PM2.5-eq, which the collision rule reads as agreement once all three are on one flow.

expectations.title: Stepwise's three PM10 spellings reach one substance
expectations.comment: Plain, mobile and stationary. Three substances on the build of 944b274.

expectations.title: Stepwise's `Particulates` and `Particulates, unspecified` reach the size-unstated total
expectations.comment: Six rows, three windows: PM2.5, PM10 and the unsized total. The same claim #153 makes about BAFU's rows, now for the list whose factors made the unsized pair a question.

expectations.title: AGRIBALYSE's `Particulates, diesel soot` lands on PM0.2 - PM2.5
expectations.comment: The owner's ruling of 2 September 2026 (plans/particle-family.md section 4): diesel exhaust particles are fine particulate, almost entirely below 2.5 um and above the 0.2 um ultrafine cut. A substance of its own on the build of 944b274, left to #190 group J.

expectations.title: AGRIBALYSE's `Particulates, SPM` lands on the size-unstated total
expectations.comment: Suspended particulate matter is a sampling term that states no cut, so it is read with `Particulates` and `Particulates, unspecified`. The owner's ruling of 2 September 2026.

expectations.title: No row of any list stating a particle size cut creates a substance
expectations.comment: The guard's claim, stated on the outcome rather than on the guard: a row the table has not read stops the build, so a build that finished read every one. Every row stating a cut spells it with ` um`; the two rows that state none -- BAFU's `Particulates` and `Particulates, unspecified` -- are the ones that mint the size-unstated total, which EF has no flow for, and are `created` by design, as #153's own claim on them says. Two `created` rows with a cut on the build of 944b274, Stepwise's PM10 strays.

expectations.title: The substance `Particulates, < 10 Um` is no longer published
expectations.comment: Minted by Stepwise's plain row on every five-list build up to 944b274. Its identifier is retired, and resolves to nothing, because the substance did not move -- it was never a substance of ours.

expectations.title: `Particles (PM10)` publishes `Particulates, < 10 um` as an alternative label
expectations.comment: On the build of 944b274 PM10 carried only `Particulates, < 10 um (stationary)`: the plain spelling was the name of Stepwise's stray substance, so the member-name pass refused it. Now stated by particulate-size-classes.json and written by the layering with its own provenance, so it is there whichever vendor's rows reached the window.

expectations.title: `Particles (PM2.5 - PM10)` publishes `Particulates, > 2.5 um, and < 10um` as an alternative label
expectations.comment: Already true on the build of 944b274 through the member-name pass, and now a promise rather than a happenstance.

expectations.title: `Particles (> PM10)` publishes `Particulates, > 10 um` as an alternative label
expectations.comment: On the build of 944b274 the window carried ecoinvent's `Particulate Matter, > 10 um` and AGRIBALYSE's `(process)` variant, and not the plain ecoinvent-2 spelling three lists ship.

expectations.title: `Particles (PM0.2)` publishes `Particulates, < 0.2 um` as an alternative label
expectations.comment: No vendor ships this spelling; it is coined on the ecoinvent-2 pattern because the rule is *always*, and a window that answered to no `Particulates` spelling would be the one a reader searching that way could not find.

expectations.title: The coarse band in urban ground-level air is worth what PM10 is worth there, under EF 3.1

subject.context_display: Environmental → Air → Ground level → Urban (>1000 people/square mile)

expectations.comment: EF 3.1 states nothing for its own coarse-band flow in any compartment and 5.48544e-5 for PM10 here; the ecoinvent Centre and GreenDelta both give the coarse band that number, and until this rule ecoinvent's rows got it through #37's override while BAFU's and AGRIBALYSE's identical rows scored zero. The owner's ruling of 2 September 2026, with the limitations page's double-count concern recorded beside the rule. `carried` while #37's rows stood (stage 2); `ruled` since stage 3 retired them, because ecoinvent's coarse rows then land here and the ecoinvent Centre's transcription states the number itself -- a stated number outranks a carried one, so the same ruling is written on the proposed-factor queue in lcia-factor-rulings.json for the four compartments ecoinvent states.

expectations.title: The coarse band at a low rural stack is worth what PM10 is worth there, carried, under EF 3.1

subject.context_display: Environmental → Air → Low stack, <25 meters → Rural (<1000 people/square mile)

expectations.comment: A compartment no ecoinvent row reaches, so no implementation speaks and the window convention carries PM10's number: 9.02255e-7, the JRC's PM10 figure for a low rural stack. Seven of the band's eleven air compartments are carried this way on the stage-3 build; the other four are ruled, the claim above.

expectations.title: Every EF air compartment that states PM10 gives the coarse band a number
expectations.comment: `characterised` is `elementary_flows.lcia_factor_count` and keeps the JRC's meaning, so it stays false: the JRC still states nothing here, and what this list carries is its own convention. The count claim is on the factor rows; this one guards the reading.

expectations.title: Particles above ten micrometres carry no number under EF 3.1
expectations.comment: No window above it is characterised in any EF implementation, so the rule leaves it blank, and that is every publisher's answer.

expectations.title: Stepwise's particles of unstated size are worth 0.157 kg PM2.5-eq, the plain row's number
expectations.comment: Two Stepwise rows collided here on the build of 944b274 -- `Particulates` at 0.157 and `Particulates, unspecified` at 0.536, its PM10 number -- and nothing was published. Ruled by the owner on 2 September 2026: a row that stated no cut is scored as no cut, which is the plain row's total-suspended-particulate figure. Published as the implementation's own row, `sole`, because the ruling settles which of the publisher's rows is transcribed; the finding records that a person chose.

expectations.title: Stepwise's particles above ten micrometres take the unsized total's number
expectations.comment: The second half of the same ruling: the unsized total is the above-ten fraction's only broader window, and the convention carries it.

expectations.title: Stepwise's ultrafine cut takes the fine fraction's 1.0
expectations.comment: Stepwise ships no PM0.2 row; the window is EF's, and it takes PM2.5's number the way EF's own JRC scores it.

expectations.title: The coarse band's carried Stepwise number reaches rural stack air by the compartment convention

subject.context_display: Environmental → Air → Medium stack, <150 meters → Rural (<1000 people/square mile)

expectations.comment: The window carry runs first, inside unspecified air; the compartment carry then treats the number as a donor because it was carried within a compartment and not along a chain of them. Without that order the compartment convention's own rule -- nothing from a carried factor -- would leave every stratum blank.
